react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: widespread perturbation of L-tryptophan metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA (run_ramp_enrichment) identified KEGG:map00380 "Tryptophan metabolism" as the top hit with an extraordinary FDR of 9.58×10⁻¹⁵, driven by six input metabolites (L-tryptophan C00078, serotonin C00780, melatonin C01598, tryptamine C00398, indoleacetaldehyde C00637, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid C00632). MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 (the human KEGG equivalent) at p = 1.59×10⁻⁸, hitting the identical six compounds. Mummichog's m/z-direct activity analysis returned the equivalent MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism (p = 8.40×10⁻⁵) with a 13/14 metabolite overlap, adding L-tryptophan enantiomer D-tryptophan via mass resolution. In parallel, Reactome ORA flagged REACT:R-HSA-209931 "Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis" (FDR 6.64×10⁻⁸), confirming that the indoleamine neuroeffector arm of the pathway is selectively engaged. The six driver metabolites span the full tryptophan degradation arc: the upstream precursor (L-tryptophan), three decarboxylation/deamination intermediates (tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid), and two downstream neuro effectors (serotonin and melatonin). The treatment therefore appears to broadly dysregulate tryptophan catabolism, with particular impact on the serotonergic/melatonergic branch. Metabolites outside this arc — doxycycline (a tetracycline antibiotic), acrolein (an electrophilic lipid-peroxidation aldehyde), milrinone (a PDE3 inhibitor), and cytidine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (an RNA-processing intermediate) — were not captured by any paradigm and likely represent secondary or off-target signals. No competing pathway reached nominal significance across more than one tool, solidifying tryptophan metabolism as the sole cross-paradigm consensus.

RaMP multi-DB ORA reported KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism at rank 1 with FDR=9.58×10⁻¹⁵ and fold enrichment=667. MetaboAnalystR PSEA captured KEGG:hsa00380 (hsa00380) at rank 1 with p=2.01×10⁻¹⁰, and Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis reported MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism at rank 1 with p=8.40×10⁻⁵ and an overlap of 13 out of 14 pathway compounds. The six driver metabolites were all six input tryptophan-related compounds mapped to these pathways. L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) enters the pathway as the canonical substrate. Tryptamine (KEGG:C00398) and indoleacetaldehyde (KEGG:C00637) represent sequential downstream derivatives, while 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632) branches into the kynurenine shunt arm. Serotonin (KEGG:C00780) and melatonin (KEGG:C01598) form the serotonin/melatonin arm, which also maps to WP:WP550 Biogenic amine synthesis. The four non-tryptophan compounds doxycycline (KEGG:C06973), acrolein (KEGG:C01471), milrinone (KEGG:C07224), and cytidine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (KEGG:C00127) were not captured by any enrichment paradigm.
